text:
maria: Heads-up — I ran a quick profile comparing FP8/INT8/4-bit kernels with our current per-channel calibration set. Large perf variance on long sequences (2k+).
kevin: Can you paste the numbers? was expecting FP8 to win on throughput.
anika: Sequence len skew is my suspicion. Are we weighting by token freq?
maria: Paste from perf-bot below: 
perf-bot: ```SUMMARY: model=redwood-xl-13b variant=int8_calib_pc set=sample-v2 N=5000
median latency: fp8=42ms int8=55ms 4bit=38ms
99p latency: fp8=210ms int8=420ms 4bit=260ms
throughput (tokens/s): fp8=650 int8=540 4bit=690
notes: 99p spike correlated with kv-cache misses and long-prefix attention.```
sam: Hmm 99p int8 is awful. Could be quantization causing divergence on outlier channels leading to extra runtime (recomputes?)
kevin: Another suspicion: kernel selection switches at certain sequence lengths; when batch has mixed lengths we do padding + KV cache thrash. That inflates 99p for some quant modes.
anika: Agreed. Our current calibration dataset (sample-v2) oversamples short web-chat examples. Need stratified sampling by seq length and by attention-sparsity.
maria: Proposed new rule: 60% stratified by length buckets (<=128, 129-512, 513-1024, 1025-2048, >2048), 20% by domain (code, docs, chat), 20% tail hard examples (repeating tokens, adversarial prompts). Thoughts?
kevin: Sounds reasonable. Also consider per-tensor vs per-channel debate: per-channel reduces quant noise but slower quant kernels. For int8 our kernel currently uses per-tensor scaling for speed; that matches throughput but hurts 99p.
sam: On that, maybe a hybrid: per-tensor for most layers, per-channel for attention + MLP gates. Those are sensitive.
anika: Plus outlier handling: we should cap contributions from extreme activations before computing scale. Maybe 99.9th percentile clip or iterative clipping with small beta.
maria: I tried 99.9 clip vs max-based calibration on a small set: 99.9 clip reduced quality regressions by 0.8% and 99p latency improved by ~12% for int8.
perf-bot: ```CALIB_TRACE: method=percentile_clip p=99.9 layers_with_pc=attn_qkv,mlp_gate
quality_regression: -0.8% (eval set A)
latency_99p_int8: -12%
note: throughput +/-2%
```
kevin: Interesting. How do we handle outlier sequences like huge repeated numeric tables? those blow up per-channel scales.
anika: Exclude extremely low-diversity sequences from calibration (entropy filter). Also add a separate 'table-like' bucket rather than mixing them.
sam: Operationally, we need a reproducible pipeline: random seed, deterministic bucketing, and a small validation holdout to catch regressions. Also keep a binary artifact of the calibration tensors for audits.
maria: Agreed. One more wrinkle — KV warmup. For streaming use, the first tokens create many cache writes; calibration that ignores cold-cache behavior underestimates real 99p. Maybe we should include prefixes that simulate cold-starts (many short sessions concatenated). e.g. maria: `simulate_sessions(prefixes=100, avg_len=24)`
kevin: Good call. Let's propose sample-v3 with: stratified length buckets, domain buckets, entropy filter, table bucket, explicit cold-cache session simulations, and percentile clipping at 99.9 for sensitive layers.
anika: I'll draft the sampling pipeline (spark/python) and add tests for perf + quality. Sam can wire in the artifact storage.
sam: I'll add CI that runs a lightweight calibration sweep on PRs touching quant kernels. If perf regresses >5% on 99p for any prod model, fail and require an owner sign-off.
maria: (typo) meant to say: I'll run a full sweep on staging devices tomorrow and share results.
kevin: :thumbsup: please also capture kernel switch points (seq len thresholds) in the trace so we can tune batching heuristics.
anika: Will do.
maria: Thanks all — will post the sample-v3 draft by EOD and link to the artifact. :rocket:
